title: Optimization progress live panel (error vs iteration + parameters): is the run healthy?
summary: A live panel for a running optimization: the error against iteration with its stopping criteria drawn, and the parameters against iteration with their bounds. It answers whether the run is healthy and why it stopped (or should stop).

media.alt: Left panel: objective error against iteration on a log axis with a grey current-error line, a teal best-so-far staircase, a rose dashed tolerance line at 1e-3, an amber dotted vertical line at iteration 120 (maximum) and a marked point at iteration 73 where the criterion is met. Right: two small panels of parameters a and b against iteration with their bounds shaded.
media.caption: Reference render of class F7.9 (design-system gallery). The data are synthetic and exist only to demonstrate the form.

source.note: Plot class from the design system's plot taxonomy; synthetic demonstration data.

read_the_figure.question: Is the run healthy?
read_the_figure.axes: Left: iteration (0 to 230) against objective error (log, about 2e-4 to 4). Right: iteration against parameter a (bounds 0 to 1) and parameter b (bounds -1 to 1), each with its bounds drawn as thin lines.
look_at: Is the best-so-far error still falling, or has it levelled off?
Which stopping criteria are drawn, and has any been met?
Are the parameters moving smoothly and settling, and are they far from their bounds?
Does the run's end agree with the criterion that is marked as met?
as_drawn: The best-so-far error falls in steps from 3 at iteration 1 to about 3e-4 at iteration 120; the current error (grey) sits above it, noisy.
The tolerance line is at 1e-3 and the maximum is 120 iterations. The best-so-far first drops below the tolerance at iteration 73 (amber dot, teal dash-dot line in every panel).
Parameter a settles near 0.26 within bounds 0 to 1 and b near 0.45 within bounds -1 to 1; both flatten by about iteration 100 and neither is near a bound.
The run log continues to iteration 120 although the criterion was met at 73: either the run is not enforcing the tolerance or the snapshot shows a run that kept going; the panel does not say which.
read_the_figure.proves: A flat best-so-far, parameters inside their bounds and a stopping criterion that is met together say that the run has converged and ended for the right reason. The panel is a status report, not a proof that the optimum is global.
if_wrong: Best-so-far still falling at the iteration limit: the run was stopped too early; raise the limit.
A parameter on a bound: the optimum may lie outside the allowed range.
A criterion met but the run continues: the stopping test is not wired in.
must_check: stop criteria drawn: without them the reader cannot tell why the run stopped or whether it should have.

terms.meaning: One update of the optimizer, usually one or a few objective evaluations.
The objective at the latest iterate, which can fluctuate.
The smallest error seen up to iteration k.
The error level below which the run is considered converged.
A hard cap that stops the run whatever the error.
The allowed range of a parameter.

remember: Stop when best-so-far < tol or k = k_max, whichever comes first.
Best-so-far is monotone; the current error need not be.
For a geometric convergence e_k = e_0 exp(-k / tau): k_stop = tau ln(e_0 / tol).
A parameter at its bound is a warning.
Draw the criteria on the plot.

understand.title: Marks and encodings
understand.text: The big panel plots the error against the iteration count on a log scale, in grey for the current value and in bold teal for the best so far. Two horizontal and vertical lines mark the two stopping criteria and an amber dot the place where the first was met. The small panels plot each parameter in blue with its bounds as thin grey lines and shaded in between; a vertical dash-dot line repeats the iteration of the stop in every panel.

understand.title: Why this form answers the question
understand.text: Plain language: while a long computation runs you want to know three things: is it still improving, will it stop, and are the numbers sensible. This panel puts all three in one glance: the staircase says improving or not, the criterion lines say how far from stopping, and the parameter panels say whether the values are sane. A live panel is a dashboard for a run.

understand.title: How it misleads
understand.text: A log axis makes a staircase of tiny improvements at 3e-4 look as important as the early drops. The best-so-far hides the noisy current error and can mask a divergence of the iterate. Showing a stop criterion as met while the run continues, as here, signals a wiring error or a misleading snapshot. And a converged run may be at a local minimum: the panel does not know.

understand.title: Alternatives
understand.text: A table of the final values, the number of iterations and the reason for stopping is compact. For stochastic runs, a band over repeats (F7.1). For slow runs, a plot of the improvement per iteration shows stagnation earlier than the error itself.

understand.title: A variant to create
understand.text: Mark the stop iteration with a vertical line that ends the curve, add the gradient norm in a third panel, and colour the parameter panel red when a parameter is within 5 percent of a bound.

steps.title: A stopping rule
steps.note: In the render the first condition is met at k = 73, well before k_max = 120.

steps.title: Predicting the stop for geometric convergence
steps.note: With e_0 = 2.5, tau = 9 and tol = 1e-3 this gives 70; the render's noisy run stops at 73.

steps.title: Why a tighter tolerance may never be met
steps.note: The best-so-far in the render levels at about 3e-4, so a tolerance of 1e-4 would end the run by the iteration limit.

worked.title: Reading the run panel in the reference render
worked.problem: (1) At which iteration does the tolerance criterion trigger and what is the error then? (2) Is the run healthy at the end? (3) What would happen with a tolerance of 1e-4?

solution.text: (1) The amber dot sits at iteration 73, at an error of about 1e-3 (just below the tolerance). The geometric model predicts a similar value.

(2) The best-so-far levels near 3e-4 from about iteration 100, parameter a is settling near 0.26 and b near 0.45, both well inside their bounds: the run looks converged. But the log continues for 47 iterations beyond the stop at 73, which should be explained.
(3) The best error never goes below about 3e-4, so a tolerance of 1e-4 is never met; the run would end at the cap of 120 iterations.

worked.answer: The tolerance is met at iteration 73 (the model predicts 70); the run looks healthy but should have stopped there; a tolerance of 1e-4 would end at the 120-iteration cap.

analyze.q: The criterion is met at iteration 73, yet the log goes on to 120. List two explanations.
analyze.hint: Check the code path of the stopping test; how was the snapshot taken?

analyze.q: Why is the best-so-far a staircase while the current error is jagged?
What would you add to detect that an optimizer is stagnating before the iteration limit?
analyze.hint: Improvement per iteration or the gradient norm.

evaluate.q: The parameters are inside the bounds and the error is below tolerance. Is the optimum found?

create: Redraw with the run ending at the stop iteration and the parameters shown relative to their bounds as a fraction.
Add a third small panel with the gradient norm and its own stop criterion.

checks.q: Why does the best-so-far curve never go up?
checks.answer: It is the smallest error seen so far, so it can only stay the same or drop.

checks.q: Geometric convergence e_k = 4 exp(-k / 12) and tolerance 1e-3. After how many iterations does the run stop?
checks.answer: k = 12 ln(4000) = 12 x 8.29 = 99.5, so about 100 iterations.

checks.q: A parameter sits exactly on its upper bound for the last 40 iterations while the error is still falling. What does it suggest?
checks.answer: The bound is active: the unconstrained optimum probably lies outside the allowed range, so the result depends on the bound; check whether the bound is physical or should be widened.
